title: Scale Agentic Coding Workflows with Meta’s Muse Spark Open on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: Meta's Muse Spark Open, an 816B MoE coding model (42B active, 1M context, multimodal), was trained on and is optimized for NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 with NVFP4 checkpoints, with NVIDIA claiming up to 50K tokens/s per GPU and tooling via Dynamo, NIM and NeMo.

insights.claim: Meta's Muse Spark Open is a coding-optimized 816B-parameter mixture-of-experts reasoning model that activates 42B parameters per token via top-8 routing across 256 experts, offering a 1M-token context window.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Sparse activation gives frontier-scale capability at a fraction of dense-model serving cost.

insights.claim: Muse Spark Open was trained on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 Blackwell Ultra systems specifically for agentic coding rather than single-shot completions.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Even Meta, which builds its own silicon, used NVIDIA rack-scale systems for this training run.
insights.locator: Trained on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 Blackwell Ultra specifically for agentic coding workflows

insights.claim: Agentic coding differs from general code completion because it needs multifile refactors, navigation of thousands of files, recovery from failing tests and subagent coordination over long horizons.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Long-horizon agent workloads consume far more tokens and context than autocomplete, expanding inference demand.
insights.quote: Agentic coding demands something fundamentally different.

insights.claim: The model uses goal conditioning and context compaction to sustain long sessions, generates commentary before each action, and offers web search, subagent spawning and computer use across desktop, mobile and browser.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Feature set puts an open model in direct competition with closed coding agents.
insights.locator: Beyond coding, it searches the web

insights.claim: A 1.8B perception encoder natively processes interleaved text, images, video frames and audio in a single pass, which suits workflows spanning screenshots, error logs and video walkthroughs.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Native multimodality extends coding agents to debugging from screen recordings.

insights.claim: GB300 NVL72 links 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs in one NVLink domain at 130 TB/s, which NVIDIA says removes the bottleneck of expert traffic crossing off-the-shelf networks and directly determines realized throughput for sparse MoE models.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Rack-scale interconnect is the moat argument for NVIDIA in serving large MoE models versus commodity networking.
insights.locator: Muse Spark Open optimized performance on GB300 NVL72

insights.claim: Out of the box on GB300 NVL72, agentic workloads reach up to 50K tokens per second per GPU and up to 600 tokens per second per user, with speculative decode on four Blackwell GPUs.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Vendor-reported throughput benchmark to compare against rival accelerators.
insights.locator: Running agentic workloads on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72

insights.claim: NVFP4 checkpoints generated by Meta shrink the memory footprint of all 816B parameters, moving fewer bytes per token and freeing memory for larger KV cache for concurrent long-context sessions, lowering cost per token.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: FP4 support ties open-model economics to Blackwell Ultra hardware.

insights.claim: NVIDIA supports SGLang, vLLM and TensorRT LLM, and Dynamo recipes for all three that separate prefill from decode on dedicated GPU pools and route requests with KV-cache-aware routing to workers already holding the prefix.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Disaggregated serving and KV-aware routing are the software layer sustaining NVIDIA's inference advantage.
insights.locator: Flexible deployment options for Muse Spark Open

insights.claim: Developers can post-train the model with NeMo AutoModel (full SFT and LoRA, native Hugging Face checkpoints) and convert to Megatron format with Megatron Bridge for large-scale training; a downloadable NIM reduces deployment to a single command.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: NVIDIA wraps open models in its own training and deployment tooling, deepening stickiness.
insights.locator: Post-train Muse Spark Open with NeMo AutoModel and Megatron Bridge
